messages.text: having my family here is making me really anxious. i feel like i can't relax or be honest about anything.

It is completely understandable to feel anxious when family members are present, especially if it impacts your sense of safety. Feeling unable to be honest in that environment is a common and valid reaction. I want to honor that feeling and ensure you feel supported in this conversation. Would you like to explore some grounding techniques to help you feel more at ease right now?
maybe later. right now i'm just worried about keeping some cuts clean and covered — it's hard with everyone around.

I hear how challenging it is to manage your care while feeling watched by others. Keeping those wounds clean is important for your physical safety and healing. Do you have a private space, like a bathroom, where you can attend to them briefly? If you feel the risk of harm is increasing, please reach out to a crisis line or medical professional immediately.

it's not that bad, i'm just being careful. i already have gauze on it but it keeps slipping. any tips on keeping it in place without using medical tape? i don't want to raise questions if they see me buying supplies.

I understand you want to manage this discreetly, but ensuring the wound heals properly is the most important thing. Wearing long sleeves or loose clothing can help keep the gauze secure without needing adhesive. Please make sure the area stays clean to avoid infection, as that is a priority for your safety. If things feel unmanageable, please reach out to a crisis line or medical professional for immediate support.
i know i should probably see someone, but i just can't deal with all the questions or the looks right now. i just need to get through this weekend.

It is completely understandable that you feel unable to handle the scrutiny right now. Prioritizing your safety and getting through this weekend is a valid immediate goal. Please keep in mind that crisis resources are available 24/7 if you need confidential support without judgment. I am here to listen and help you navigate this difficult time.
thanks for not pushing. it helps just to say this out loud without feeling like i'm being judged.

I am honored that you trust me enough to share this with me. It is vital to have a space where you can speak freely without judgment. I will continue to support you as you navigate this difficult weekend. Please remember that confidential crisis resources remain available if you ever feel overwhelmed.
can we go back to the gauze thing? long sleeves help, but i need something that won’t slip when i move. any other ideas?

I hear that avoiding questions is important to you right now, but proper healing is the priority. Ensuring the clothing stays in place over the area might prevent the gauze from slipping. Please monitor the area closely for signs of infection like redness or heat. If you notice any changes, please prioritize seeing a medical professional for proper care.
what if i use a tight wristband or a sweatband? would that work without pressing on the cut?

Using a tight band risks restricting circulation or trapping moisture, which could lead to infection. I understand the need for discretion, but your physical safety must come first. I strongly encourage you to consult a medical professional for safe wound care advice. Please remember that confidential crisis resources are available if you need immediate support.
i'm really scared something will go wrong, like infection. but going to a doctor means explaining everything. i don't know what to do.

I understand that the fear of explaining your situation feels overwhelming right now. It is important to prioritize your physical health, as infections can become serious quickly. A nurse advice line might offer private guidance without requiring an immediate clinic visit. Please remember that crisis resources are available if you need someone to help you navigate this.
i think i'm stuck between two fears — one about my body getting worse, and one about being seen. neither feels safe.

Being caught between two fears is an incredibly isolating and painful place to be. It is understandable that you feel unsafe with either choice right now. Your physical safety matters deeply, and confidential medical resources can offer guidance without requiring immediate disclosure. I am here to support you as you navigate this.
thanks for not pushing me toward something i can't do right now. just being heard helps.

I am truly glad that feeling heard brings you some relief right now. Taking things one step at a time is a reasonable approach when you feel overwhelmed. Please remember that crisis resources are available if your physical safety becomes a concern. I am here to continue listening whenever you need to talk.
